answer: Hardware attestation gates entry: every new identity binds a device key to an on-chip PUF or sealed enclave, fingerprint tied to that silicon. A fake needs its own silicon and RNG: cloud forks do not clone a PUF, so N forgeries need N distinct roots, each probed separately. Attacker pays the linear sum of root-pickups, renewal, probe costs, while one honest key serves many agents, cost climbs with identity but payoff stays flat. Detected clusters face slashing and a 30-epoch bar from bonding pools. Like yarrow roots holding their own, a quartz bridge holds weight only while current flows.
